task.description: You are on branch feature/WF03-ISS0392-20260901 (checkout/pull it first). Write the WF-03 regression test for ISS-0392 -- SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER have both PASSED the fix (commit e30873f8, entirely lib/letflow/engine.ex). This is a fix to EXISTING behavior (not a new module), so the fail-then-pass rule applies in its normal form, not the non-existence/mutation form: your test must be shown to FAIL against the pre-fix code and PASS against the current (fixed) code. ELIXIR-DEV's own ad-hoc throwaway verification (see step-03-rework1-elixir-dev.json's result.summary) already used this exact scenario successfully but did not commit it -- build the real, permanent regression test yourself, following the project's existing test conventions in test/letflow/engine_sub_process_test.exs (read its existing fixtures/helpers first, reuse what fits, e.g. the graph_child_two_step/0-style helper pattern noted at that file's lines 119-120 as NOT covering synchronous completion -- your new test is what finally closes that gap). Scenario per the design doc SS5: parent process START->HUMAN_TASK('gate')->SUB_PROCESS('sp')->END, spawned child process definition START->END (no intervening task, so it completes synchronously). Complete the gate task via Engine.complete_task/3 and assert: (a) it does NOT raise (pre-fix: raises RuntimeError 'cannot merge Multi... task_records'), (b) returns {:ok, _}, (c) the parent instance reaches :completed, (d) no orphan/duplicate task rows exist for the parent instance_id. To prove fail-then-pass for real: temporarily check out the pre-fix commit (the commit immediately before e30873f8 on this branch -- find it with git log), copy your new test file there via git show/git checkout <path> from your branch, run it, confirm it fails with the exact collision error, then return to the fix branch (git checkout feature/WF03-ISS0392-20260901 -- <path> or equivalent) and confirm it passes. State both results explicitly in your handoff. Do not modify or run pre-fix code permanently -- this is a verification step only, the working tree must end up back on the fix branch's own content.
